note: Classification rules, evaluated in order - first match wins, so specific rules go above general ones. Every rule ID appears in the audit trail against the transactions it classified, so IDs must be stable and meaningful. Anything no rule matches goes to suspense (9000) for a person to decide; that queue is the work, not a failure.

rules.note: Residential rent - property income, exempt for VAT
Commercial rent - check whether the option to tax has been exercised

Deductible in full - s.24 applies only to residential. MUST be evaluated before the general mortgage interest rule below, because the first match wins and 'COMMERCIAL MORTGAGE INTEREST' also contains 'MORTGAGE INTEREST'. Ordering these the other way round silently posts commercial interest to the restricted account and overstates the tax.
RESTRICTED under s.24 - relief is a 20% tax reducer, not a deduction
CAPITAL - improves the property beyond its previous condition. Not deductible against rent; increases the CGT base cost. Keep the invoice permanently.
Revenue repair - restores rather than improves. Query anything large.
PAYE and NIC must have been operated on this

deliberately_unmatched: There is no rule for 'TRANSFER MAINTENANCE SERVICES', 'COUNTER CREDIT CASH' or 'PAYMENT R MEHRA CONSULTANCY' in the example data. That is intentional. Each needs a human decision - is it an expense, drawings, a related-party payment requiring disclosure, or unrecorded income? Writing a rule to sweep them into a category would make the books look finished while making them wrong.
